A.biggest_strength: Allows students to enter arbitrary custom values for client/server ISNs and payload length to dynamically test sequence arithmetic.
A.biggest_weakness: Poor mobile responsiveness where the diagram overflows horizontally, cutting off the entire server lifeline and state badges on phone screens.

B.biggest_strength: Masterful pedagogical framing centered around the color-coded unifying formula ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN, accompanied by live endpoint TCB variables (SND.NXT/RCV.NXT) and verified Linux kernel packet captures.
B.biggest_weakness: Lacks freeform input fields for students to type arbitrary sequence numbers or payload sizes, offering only three curated presets.

structured_output.reasons: Page B is substantially better suited for a networking class. It crystallizes the core mechanism of TCP sequence and acknowledgment calculation into an elegant, color-coded equation (ack = seq + len + SYN + FIN) that clearly demonstrates why SYN and FIN consume sequence space while pure ACKs do not. Furthermore, B visualizes the internal endpoint state tracking variables (SND.NXT and RCV.NXT), incorporates verified real-world Linux capture data, and seamlessly reflows its layout on mobile devices, whereas Page A's diagram is cut off on phone screens.
